bib.title: Star Attention: Efficient LLM Inference over Long Sequences
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), Vancouver, PMLR 267, 2025

read.skipped: Reference list (about chars 37000-43000) skimmed only; no body or appendix text skipped.

question: Can long-context inference be sped up across multiple hosts, with no fine-tuning, by encoding the context with blockwise-local attention and using global attention only for the query and generated tokens?
hypothesis: Context tokens need only attend to nearby tokens while query tokens need to attend to all prior tokens, so a two-phase block-sparse approximation keeps accuracy close to global attention.
contributions: Star Attention: a two-phase block-sparse approximation (blockwise-local context encoding with anchor blocks, then sequence-global query encoding and generation) that shards attention across hosts
Distributed softmax aggregation that communicates one vector and one scalar per token per host instead of moving KV cache
Evaluation on RULER, BABILong and InfiniteBench with Llama-3/3.1 8B and 70B, up to 1M tokens, against Ring Attention, StreamingLLM and MInference
Ablation of anchor block position, content and size

method.summary: Phase 1 splits the context into contiguous blocks of b tokens, prefixes each block except the first with the first block (anchor block, original position ids kept), has each host compute attention over its 2b tokens without cross-host communication, keeps the KV of the non-anchor block and discards anchor KV. Phase 2 broadcasts the query to all hosts, each attends to its local KV, and a designated query host combines local outputs A_h and softmax denominators s_h via online softmax (log-sum-exp) into global attention, generates tokens and is the only host that appends to its KV cache. Applied to pretrained Llama models with no fine-tuning, using Flash Attention per host.
method.task: long-context inference efficiency (prefill and decode over 16K to 1M token inputs)

datasets.name: RULER
datasets.preprocessing: Ablations use four NIAH tasks (Single 2, Single 3, MultiKey 1, MultiQuery) with Paul Graham essays as haystack

datasets.name: InfiniteBench
datasets.size: 10 tasks as evaluated in Table 3 (Table 10 lists 12 rows)
datasets.split: average input from 43.9k to 2068.6k tokens by task

inference.prompting: Base models: {context}{query}{answer prefix}. Instruct models: Llama-3 chat template with system message 'You are a helpful assistant.'; context goes in Phase 1, query and answer prefix in Phase 2 (answer prefix only for RULER).

parameters.block_size: one-quarter of sequence length (4K at 16K, 8K at 32K, 16K at 64K, 32K at 128K); fixed 32K for sequences over 128K
parameters.anchor_block_size: equal to context block size; first block of the sequence; position ids kept as 0..b-1
parameters.kernel: Flash Attention per host with log-sum-exp online softmax aggregation
parameters.streamingllm_baseline: 1000 global sink tokens plus 8000 token sliding window
parameters.minference_baseline: three sparse patterns, best pattern per head chosen by offline search
parameters.gpus_and_workers: 8B: 16K-128K 8 GPUs 4 workers; 256K-512K 16 GPUs 8 workers; 1M 32 GPUs 16 workers. 70B: 16K-32K 8 GPUs 4 workers; 64K 16 GPUs 4 workers; 128K 32 GPUs 8 workers

other.implementation: HuggingFace Transformers (reported) and NVIDIA TRT-LLM (similar relative trends)

metrics.name: benchmark accuracy
metrics.definition: task accuracy on RULER, BABILong, InfiniteBench; Star Attention reported as absolute difference from Ring Attention (Table 1)

metrics.name: relative speedup
metrics.definition: inference speed of Star Attention relative to Ring Attention

metrics.name: time per sample
metrics.definition: wall-clock seconds per sample on 8 A100 GPUs

eval.protocol: Single reported number per setting; no seeds, variance or significance test stated. Speedup measured only against Ring Attention; accuracy against all three baselines.

availability.weights: uses public Llama and Gradient.ai checkpoints

results.claim: Star Attention reaches up to 11x speedup over Ring Attention while keeping 97-100% of accuracy.
results.setup: RULER, Llama-3-8B-Instruct-1048K, block size 32K fixed, sequence lengths above 128K; accuracy retention 97-100% stated in abstract for the main configs
results.quote: reducing memory requirements and inference time by up to 11x while preserving 97-100% of accuracy
results.note: Abstract says 11x; Section 3.4 and Table 5 report 10.8x at 256K and 16.9x at 1M.

results.claim: At 1M tokens speedup rises to 16.9x with a 5.32% accuracy drop.
results.setup: RULER, Llama-3-8B-Instruct-1048K, 1M tokens, block size 32K, vs Ring Attention, 32 A100 GPUs 16 workers
results.quote: At 1M tokens, the speedup increases to 16.9× with an accuracy drop of just 5.32%.

results.claim: On Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct at 64K, Star Attention is 4.7x faster than Ring Attention with a 1.44% accuracy drop.
results.setup: RULER, 64K, block size 16K, anchor 16K, 16 GPUs 4 workers
results.quote: the Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct model exhibits a 4.7× acceleration at 64K tokens with minimal accuracy drop

results.claim: At 128K on the 70B model speedup is 8.7x but accuracy drops 7.47%.

results.table: Table 5, row Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct 128K, columns Seq. Len. 128, Block Size 16, Ring-Attn 65.29, DAcc -7.47%, DSpeedup 8.7x

results.setup: RULER, block size 1/4 of length; Ring-Attn accuracy at 128K 76.31%, Star delta -1.90%

results.table: Table 2, row Star Attention, column Average

results.claim: At 128K on RULER, Star Attention scores 74.41 versus MInference 58.17 and full attention 76.31.
On InfiniteBench Star Attention averages 46.51 versus 48.06 full attention, 34.07 MInference and 14.72 StreamingLLM.

The text claims Star Attention 'excels especially in retrieval-heavy tasks' but it is below full attention there.

results.claim: Larger block size improves accuracy; one-quarter of sequence length is the recommended trade-off, and accuracy degrades with smaller blocks on longer sequences.
Without instruction tuning the Llama-3.1-8B base model shows anomalies on BABILong under Star Attention, at longer sequence lengths.

limits: Multi-hop tracing degrades because context blocks cannot attend to each other during Phase 1; the authors call cross-block communication future work.
Accuracy degrades when blocks are small relative to long sequences (-6.73% at 512K, -7.47% at 128K on 70B with block 16K).
Why anchor size must equal context block size is not explained; authors say it is left for future work.
The attention-sink explanation for anchors is a conjecture; the anchor size ablation suggests other factors.
Speedups are measured only against Ring Attention; vanilla causal generation OOMs beyond 64K on 8 A100s in the HF implementation, which lacks multi-node support.
Below about 32K tokens distributed methods are not faster than vanilla.
No variance, seeds or significance tests; decoding settings not stated.
Speedup applies to context encoding and query decoding on a multi-host setup; single-GPU benefits not evaluated.
Prompt structure assumes a long context followed by a short query and short answer.

terms.definition: the first block c1 of the sequence, prefixed to every other context block during Phase 1 so attention sinks shift to anchor tokens; its KV is discarded after encoding
the designated host that aggregates local attention outputs and softmax sums from all hosts in Phase 2, generates tokens and is the only host updating its KV cache

lineage.note: distributed global attention baseline for speedups; Star Attention drops the ring communication during context encoding
sparse attention baseline and source of the attention sink explanation
used per host for local attention
